name: ctrnn-parameter-space
title: CTRNN Parameter-Space Structure
lead:
Before a CTRNN can steer a body through an environment it must have dynamics
worth steering with. This investigation characterises the bare brain: the
equilibria, their stability, and the bifurcations that reshape them, for the
smallest CTRNNs. It is the dynamical-systems foundation every embodied Beer
model in this repository builds on.

glossary.definition: Continuous-time recurrent neural network; τ_i ẏ_i = −y_i + Σ_j w_ij σ(y_j+θ_j) + I_i.
Bias set so each neuron's sigmoid is centered given its total input: θ_i = −Σ_j w_ij/2.
A bifurcation where two equilibria (one stable, one unstable) are created or annihilated.
A symmetry-breaking bifurcation: one equilibrium becomes three (the central one loses stability, two symmetric stable ones appear).
Codimension-2 point where two saddle-node fold curves meet; the center-crossing pitchfork is its symmetric axis.
Structure seen when two parameters vary; here the cusp organising the fold curves.

biological_story:
A continuous-time recurrent neural network is the minimal nervous system Beer
evolves for his model agents: each neuron integrates weighted sigmoidal input
from the others toward an equilibrium set by its bias and self-connection.
Whether such a network can latch a decision, hold a memory, or generate a
rhythm is a question about its dynamics, not its wiring diagram alone. A single
neuron with strong self-excitation becomes bistable — two stable rest states
separated by an unstable threshold — the dynamical substrate of a binary
memory. Where exactly that bistability switches on, as the self-weight and bias
vary, traces a cusp in parameter space. Two neurons coupled with opposite-sign
reciprocal connections can instead destabilise their shared equilibrium and
circle it forever — a central pattern generator in miniature. These are the
dynamical building blocks the embodied agents in this repository recruit.
question:
How is the dynamical repertoire of a small continuous-time recurrent neural
network (CTRNN) — the "brain" shared by all of Beer's brain-body-environment
agents — organized as a function of its parameters (self-weights and biases)?
Where do equilibria appear and disappear, and what is the codimension-1 and
codimension-2 structure of those bifurcations?
hypothesis:
A single self-excitatory center-crossing neuron undergoes a pitchfork
bifurcation from one equilibrium to three (bistability) as its self-weight
increases past w≈4 (on the symmetric center-crossing line). Off that line the
pitchfork unfolds into two saddle-node (fold) curves that bound a cusp-shaped
bistable wedge in the (self-weight, bias) plane and meet at a cusp — the
codimension-2 organizing structure described by Beer (2006, 2022). A two-neuron center-crossing
circuit with mixed-sign mutual coupling can lose stability of its interior
equilibrium and oscillate.

executive.what_is_this:
A brain-only study of CTRNN dynamics — no body, no environment. We compute
equilibria, Jacobian eigenvalues, nullclines, and bifurcation structure for
1- and 2-neuron CTRNNs, reproducing the parameter-space picture from Beer
(2006, 2022).
executive.verdict:
The expected pitchfork / bistability structure is reproduced: a single
center-crossing neuron goes 1→3 equilibria (pitchfork, w≈4) with increasing
self-weight, the bistable region forms a wedge in (w, θ) bounded by
saddle-node folds meeting at a cusp, and a 2-neuron center-crossing
circuit oscillates (interior equilibrium unstable).
executive.verdict_detail:
All three studies' acceptance behaviours hold from the workspace's own
numpy/scipy analysis code (equilibria via multi-start root finding, stability
via Jacobian eigenvalues), verified in the test suite.

scientific_argument.main_claim:
The equilibrium structure of small center-crossing CTRNNs is organised by a
cusp: on the symmetric center-crossing line a pitchfork creates bistability,
which off-axis unfolds into two saddle-node fold curves meeting at the cusp,
exactly as Beer's
parameter-space analysis predicts.
evidence_for: Single-neuron pitchfork (center-crossing): 1 equilibrium at self-weight 1.0, 3 at 8.0.
Codim-2 (w, θ) map shows a connected bistable wedge bounded by two saddle-node fold curves meeting at a cusp.
2-neuron center-crossing circuit [[4.5,1],[-1,4.5]] sustains oscillation; interior equilibrium is unstable.
key_figures: figures/phase_portrait.png — 2-neuron phase portrait with nullclines + equilibrium
figures/bifurcation.png — codim-1 pitchfork (center-crossing), 1→3 equilibria vs self-weight
figures/codim2.png — codim-2 equilibrium-count map over (w, θ)
caveats: Equilibria are found by multi-start root finding; counts depend on search breadth (fixed seed used).
This is pure brain dynamics; embodied consequences are studied in the other investigations.

studies.name: param-space-equilibria-and-nullclines
studies.title: Equilibria, Nullclines & Oscillation (2-neuron)
studies.question:
What is the phase-plane geometry of a two-neuron center-crossing CTRNN with
mixed-sign reciprocal coupling — where are its nullclines and equilibrium, and
is that equilibrium stable or does the circuit oscillate?

findings.summary: Single interior equilibrium, unstable; circuit oscillates (tail range ≈ 0.62).
findings.detail:
Phase portrait (figures/phase_portrait.png) shows the two nullclines crossing
at one interior point marked as unstable; the vector field circulates around
it, consistent with the sustained oscillation measured in the suite.

studies.claim:
The 2-neuron center-crossing circuit has a single unstable interior
equilibrium and oscillates — a minimal central pattern generator.

derived.insight: Single interior equilibrium, unstable; circuit oscillates (tail range ≈ 0.62).

studies.name: param-space-codim1-bifurcations
studies.title: Codim-1 Pitchfork: 1→3 Equilibria (Beer 2006)
studies.question:
As the self-weight of a single center-crossing CTRNN neuron increases, how does
its equilibrium set change, and at what point does bistability appear?

findings.summary: Pitchfork confirmed (center-crossing slice): 1 equilibrium at w=1.0, 3 at w=8.0 (two stable, one unstable).
findings.detail:
The bifurcation diagram (figures/bifurcation.png), on the center-crossing
symmetric slice, shows the single branch splitting symmetrically into three
at w≈4 as self-weight increases, with the middle branch unstable (red) and
the outer branches stable (black).

studies.claim:
On the center-crossing (symmetric, θ=−w/2) slice, a single neuron undergoes a
pitchfork bifurcation at w≈4 from 1 to 3 equilibria as self-weight grows,
reproducing Beer (2006). Off this slice the pitchfork unfolds into saddle-node
folds (see the codim-2 study).

derived.insight: Pitchfork confirmed (center-crossing slice): 1 equilibrium at w=1.0, 3 at w=8.0 (two stable, one unstable).

studies.name: param-space-codim2-structure
studies.title: Codim-2 Bistability Wedge (Beer 2022)
studies.question:
How is the single-neuron 1→3 transition organised (saddle-node fold curves and a cusp) when both the self-weight
and the bias vary — what is the shape of the bistable region in the
(self-weight, bias) plane?

findings.summary: Connected bistable wedge found; max equilibrium count = 3 over the grid.
findings.detail:
The codim-2 map (figures/codim2.png) shows a yellow (3-equilibria) wedge
opening at high self-weight and bounded by two fold curves meeting at a cusp, with a boundary
cell at exactly 2 equilibria sitting on the fold.

studies.claim:
Bistability occupies a connected cusp wedge in (self-weight, bias), reproducing
the codim-2 structure of Beer (2022).

derived.insight: Connected bistable wedge found; max equilibrium count = 3 over the grid.
